etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English norischen, from Old French nouriss-, stem of one of the conjugated forms of norrir, from Latin nutriō (“to suckle, feed, foster, nourish, cherish, preserve, support”).

definitions.definition: (transitive) To feed and cause to grow; to supply with food or other matter which increases weight and promotes health.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Isaiah 44:14:
quote.text: He planteth an ash, and the rain doth nourish it.

quote.citation: 1623, Francis Bacon, Historia Vitae et Mortis:
quote.text: other carnivorous Animals are difficultly nourished by Plants alone

quote.citation: 1872, Thomas Bull, The Maternal Management of Children, in Health and Diseases:
quote.text: Children nourished exclusively upon this simple food will be found to enjoy more perfect health

quote.citation: 1996, Alexander Frank Skutch, Orioles, Blackbirds, and Their Kin: A Natural History:
quote.text: we have ample evidence that male Bobolinks do not shirk the labor of nourishing their families. In a four-year study, Wittenberger (1980, 1982) found that males delivered about 60 Bobolink percent of the food.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To support; to maintain; to be responsible for.

quote.citation: 1591 (date written), William Shakespeare, “The Second Part of Henry the Sixt, […]”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies. […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act III, scene i]:
quote.text: I in Ireland nourish a mighty band.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To encourage; to foster; to stimulate

quote.citation: 2003, Marilyn Byfield Paul, It's Hard to Make a Difference When You Can't Find Your Keys:
quote.text: When we slow down to pay attention to our own experience, we open ourselves to the love and richness that is here all the time. These are moments that can nourish your connection to your heart.

quote.citation: 2010, Colin L. Powell, My American Journey:
quote.text: I thanked the Fort Leavenworth military historian, Colonel von Schlemmer, for nourishing my first hope to memorialize the Buffalo Soldiers

definitions.definition: (transitive, of a person) To educate or bring up; to nurture; to promote emotional, spiritual or other non-physical growth.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, 1 Timothy 4:6:
quote.text: Nourished up in the words of faith.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To promote growth; to furnish nutriment.
